newsitem.title: UK: Oftel gives BT go ahead on schools cable deal.
newsitem.headline: Oftel gives BT go ahead on schools cable deal.

text.p: UK telecoms watchdog Oftel said on Wednesday that it welcomed the cable industry's new deal for schools and added there was no bar to British Telecommunications Plc competing in similar vein.
The Cable industry body announced earlier today the first ever fixed price telephony tariffs to allow unlimited use of the Internet in the classroom.
It said in a statement the deal allows schools unlimited access to the Internet with an ISDN or equivalent high-speed 64K link costing 50 pounds per month.

Cable Communications Association chairman, Stephen Davidson, said, "The internet offer builds upon the cable industry's existing commitment to provide a free standard cable connection to every school passed by the cable network, and provides a platform for the introduction of interactive and broadband services."
Oftel said the deal represents a positive step to improve schools' access to the developing range of interactive services, including appropriate use of the Internet.
It added that it was also an excellent illustration of collaboration on a strategic issue to strengthen telecoms competition in the UK.

Oftel noted that usage of the Internet and on-line technology by schools, colleges and libraries has been limited because of concern about running up large and unpredictable call bills and the need for cheaper telecommunications links offering more capacity than ordinary phone lines.
Oftel said it has written to BT setting out the rules it will apply if BT wishes to reduce its prices to schools in response to this cable deal.
